sections.h2: Sioux Falls housing at a glance
sections.html:
Sioux Falls is South Dakota's largest city and the Minnehaha County seat, with a northern slice of the city reaching into Lincoln County. It sits near the Minnesota line, where Interstate 29 meets Interstate 90. The 2020 census counted 192,517 residents, up 25.1 percent from 2010, and the Census Bureau estimates 213,748 for July 1, 2025.

Growth this fast means new subdivisions keep going up and compete with older neighborhoods for the same buyers. Health care, banking and food processing drive the job market, with Sanford Health and Avera Health at the top of the employer list. A transfer or new job at one of them is a common reason a house goes up for sale on short notice, and relocation dates rarely wait for a normal listing schedule.

sections.h2: Flood rules for Sioux Falls houses
sections.html:
A house inside a mapped floodplain carries extra permit rules, and the city applies them after storm damage. Following the flash flooding of June 2024, Planning and Development Services reminded owners that construction or repair in a floodplain needs a floodplain development permit, even where no building permit is required.

The city adds up damage over three years. Once repair costs hit 45 percent or more of the structure's pre-flood market value, work cannot begin until the owner shows the floodplain ordinance is met, which may mean elevating or flood-proofing the building. If your house is flood damaged, ask the city where that line falls before you spend money.

On insurance, the city moved to Community Rating System Class 7 on October 1, 2023, which gives 15 percent off National Flood Insurance Program premiums on covered properties. The city announcement has the current class.

Owners and managers of long-term and short-term rentals in Sioux Falls must hold a city rental permit, effective January 1, 2024, even if they registered earlier. The permit costs $50 per address, and the owner completes a one-time training course of at least two hours.

  • Get the permit before advertising, soliciting renters or allowing anyone to move in.
  • Each rental street address needs its own permit.
  • Report a change of ownership or management in writing within 30 days.
  • An owner living more than 50 miles away must name a local contact for upkeep.
  • A fourth violation can lead to revocation when three were cited in the previous three calendar years.

Transferring a permit costs nothing when written notice is given, so tell the buyer of a tenant-occupied house to file that notice. Code Enforcement also handles nuisance, property maintenance, signs, trees, grass, weeds and zoning complaints, which means a tall lawn or a debris pile can draw a citation before closing.

Three things come up in nearly every sale here: the seller's disclosure statement, the Certificate of Real Estate Value and the transfer fee. The state form, dated 07/2025, is required by law and must reach the buyer. It covers liens, easements, flood plains, the roof, water penetration, radon, lead paint, mold and about 47 systems and appliances. If a material fact changes before closing, amend it in writing.

No deed gets recorded without the Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56), which names buyer and seller, gives the legal description and states the real price and payment terms.

A house in the Lincoln County part of the city is recorded with that county's register of deeds. Check the county on your tax bill before scheduling closing.

South Dakota bills a year behind, so a seller usually owes part of the current bill at closing. Minnehaha County taxes are due January 1. The first half is accepted without penalty through April 30 and the second half through October 31, and late payments carry a 10 percent annual penalty. Unpaid tax comes out of your proceeds, and the county treasurer can give you a payoff figure.

Owner-occupied status changes the bill. The classification requires the owner to live in the home on the November 1 assessment date. After a sale, the new owner files a new application between November 1 and March 15. Our Sioux Falls property tax guide has more on assessments and levies.

Sioux Falls winters are cold, with about 25 days a year at or below zero and about 45.3 inches of snow. Freeze and thaw cycles are hard on shingles, gutters, sidewalks and foundation walls. Buyers who borrow often ask for repairs to a worn roof or a damp basement. A cash buyer generally takes those items as they are, one reason owners of houses with deferred maintenance consider that route.

sections.h2: Which way of selling fits you?
sections.html:
An agent listing usually reaches the widest pool of buyers, but it brings showings, inspections, repair requests and commission. Selling on your own saves commission and leaves you with the paperwork above. A cash offer works best when time, condition or tenants are the obstacle.

  • An inherited house with an unfinished estate
  • A rental with tenants or an unresolved permit problem
  • Flood or storm damage you cannot afford to repair
  • Back taxes or a mortgage slipping behind
  • A relocation with a fixed start date

We buy Sioux Falls houses as-is. Offers depend on the property, and you can decline at no cost.

With a cash buyer there is no appraisal, no loan underwriting and no repair negotiation. You describe the house, we make an offer, and a title company handles ownership checks, liens and closing papers. You choose the closing date. Have these ready: the deed or legal description, the tax notice, any rental permit number, and payoff details for a mortgage. If a tenant lives there, tell us the lease terms up front.

Closing costs and any back taxes are taken from the proceeds, so you do not need to bring money to the table.

faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 213,748 residents as of July 1, 2025, up from 192,517 in 2020. It is the state's largest city.

faqs.q: Does a Sioux Falls seller have to give a disclosure statement?
faqs.a: Yes. South Dakota requires sellers of real property to complete the property condition disclosure and give it to the buyer. Amend it in writing if a material fact changes before closing.

faqs.q: What is the transfer fee in Minnehaha County?
faqs.a: The county lists $1.00 per thousand, or $0.50 per $500, plus a $30.00 recording fee for a deed. SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions, such as some transfers between spouses or parent and child.

faqs.q: Do I need a rental permit to sell a tenant-occupied house?
faqs.a: The owner must hold a city permit at $50 per address. It transfers without a fee when written notice is given, and ownership changes must be reported within 30 days.

faqs.q: Can I sell with back property tax due, and which county do I pay?
faqs.a: Yes. Unpaid tax and the 10 percent annual penalty are paid from proceeds at closing. Most of the city is in Minnehaha County and a smaller part is in Lincoln County, so check your tax notice for the right treasurer.
